title: SDFGI produces no indirect lighting with the Metal renderer on Apple M5 / Apple9 GPUs
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.5.stable ~ 4.7.2.stable on Apple M5 Max
- Not reproducible in 4.4.1.stable on Apple M5 Max
- Not reproducible in 4.x on Apple M1 Max

### System information

 macOS 26.5.1 - Apple M5 Max (Apple9 GPU) - Metal - Forward+   

### Issue description


When running on an Apple M5 Max (Apple9 GPU) using the native **Metal** renderer, SDFGI produces no visible indirect lighting. Toggling SDFGI on or off produces the exact same image.

- **Expected**: SDFGI adds indirect bounce illumination to the scene (as seen in 4.4.1, with Vulkan on M5, or with Metal on M1 Max).
- **Actual**: No indirect illumination is rendered with Metal on Apple9.

*(Note: The test scene uses a `SpotLight3D`, so this is unrelated to the `AreaLight3D` physical-units issue in #122457).*

This regression appears specific to SDFGI, not to all GI implementations. A matching Cornell-box VoxelGI test on the same M5 Max produced:

| Version | VoxelGI disabled | VoxelGI enabled |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| First bad commit (`5230f6c60`) | `0.000005524130` | `0.101114476874` |
| 4.7.2.stable | `0.000005524130` | `0.101114476874` |

VoxelGI uses an `R8G8B8A8_UNORM` runtime lighting texture and does not use the affected `R32_UINT` to `RGB9E5Float` shared view.

---

#### 1. Regression Bisect

The issue was bisected between `4.4.1-stable` and `4.5-stable` to commit [`5230f6c60c`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/5230f6c60c28b1a34fb0136f84aa901afe382f39) from PR #108028 (*"Apple: Use image atomic operations on supported Apple hardware"*).

* **Before #108028**: The Metal driver added `MTLTextureUsageShaderAtomic` to every texture whose format supported atomic operations:
  ```objc
  if (@available(macOS 14.0, iOS 17.0, tvOS 17.0, *)) {
      if (format_caps & kMTLFmtCapsAtomic) {
          desc.usage |= MTLTextureUsageShaderAtomic;
      }
  }
  ```
* **After #108028**: `MTLTextureUsageShaderAtomic` is only added when `TEXTURE_USAGE_STORAGE_ATOMIC_BIT` is explicitly requested by the caller.

---

#### 2. How this affects SDFGI

SDFGI does not perform atomic operations on its light storage textures, so it does not request `TEXTURE_USAGE_STORAGE_ATOMIC_BIT`. However, removing this flag exposes a texture view issue specific to Apple9 GPUs.

SDFGI allocates two resources that share underlying storage via texture views:
- **Parent texture**: `DATA_FORMAT_R32_UINT`
- **Shared texture view**: `DATA_FORMAT_E5B9G9R9_UFLOAT_PACK32`

Source locations:
- Cascade light textures: [`gi.cpp#L478-L481`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5d63a641c79b5fb83e8d6752864c739f3254d720/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/gi.cpp#L478-L481), [`gi.cpp#L552-L560`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5d63a641c79b5fb83e8d6752864c739f3254d720/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/gi.cpp#L552-L560)
- Light probe textures: [`gi.cpp#L513-L525`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5d63a641c79b5fb83e8d6752864c739f3254d720/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/gi.cpp#L513-L525)

The compute shaders write packed light values into the `R32_UINT` parent via `imageStore()`. Subsequent passes then sample that storage through the `RGB9E5` texture view.

---

#### 3. Investigation Findings

On Apple9 GPUs, when `MTLTextureUsageShaderAtomic` is omitted from the descriptor:

1. **Parent vs View**:
   - The `R32_UINT` parent texture **contains valid non-zero data** after voxelization.
   - Reading/sampling from the shared `RGB9E5Float` view **always returns `0`** (both filtered sampling and direct texel fetches return zero).
2. **Fix verified**:
   - Adding `MTLTextureUsageShaderAtomic` back to the parent texture descriptor immediately makes the `RGB9E5` view readable again and restores SDFGI indirect lighting.
3. **Eliminated causes (do NOT fix the issue)**:
   - Explicit memory barriers / fences
   - Disabling argument buffers
   - Changing MSL target versions
   - Re-enabling SPIRV-Cross read/write texture fences
   - Disabling image atomic operations

**Why this is an Apple9 driver bug rather than UB:**
- [Apple Metal documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtltexture) explicitly states that compatible texture views share the same underlying storage, and modifications made via one texture are visible in the other.
- Godot correctly sets `MTLTextureUsagePixelFormatView`, `MTLTextureUsageShaderRead`, and `MTLTextureUsageShaderWrite` as required ([Metal doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtltextureusage/pixelformatview)).
- The exact same code works on **M1 Max (Apple7 GPU)** under the same macOS 26.5.1 version.
- On Apple9, `MTLTextureUsageShaderAtomic` changes the resource path selected by the driver. The exact internal layout or cache interaction is unknown; the test only establishes that adding the flag avoids the failure.

---


### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project on a Mac with an Apple M5 / Apple9 GPU.
2. Run using the **Metal** renderer.
3. Compare the scene with SDFGI enabled vs disabled -> **Observed**: No indirect lighting change.
4. Run the same project with **Vulkan** -> **Observed**: Indirect illumination renders as expected.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[metal-sdfgi-bisect.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31257740/metal-sdfgi-bisect.zip)
